title: Apostle to the apostles (John 20:11–18)
hookLine: Mary Magdalene is sent to tell the others; Pope Francis raised her day to a feast in 2016

cards: Early Sunday morning, still dark. Mary Magdalene has come to the tomb and found the stone rolled away. She ran for Peter and the beloved disciple.
They came running, saw the linen cloths lying there, and went home. She didn't. She's standing outside the tomb, crying.
It's the kind of crying where you can't leave, because leaving would make it real. Everyone else has gone. And she's the one who stays.

teach.b: She stoops to look into the tomb and sees two angels where the body had been. Woman, why weepest thou? Because they have taken away my Lord, she says, and I know not where they have laid him.
She turns and sees a man she takes for the gardener. Sir, if you've carried him off, tell me where, and I'll take him away.
Then he says one word. In the Douay-Rheims: "Jesus saith to her: Mary. She turning, saith to him: Rabboni (which is to say, Master)." Not a speech.
Her name. The good shepherd said his sheep know his voice when he calls them by name, and here it happens. Then Jesus says, do not touch me, for I am not yet ascended.
The Latin, noli me tangere, gave its name to many paintings.
The Greek may mean something closer to, don't hold on to me, don't cling.
Because she has a job. Go to my brethren, he says, and tell them. And she does.
The text says: Mary Magdalen cometh and telleth the disciples, "I have seen the Lord," and what he said to her. In John's telling, she's the one sent with the news, sent to the apostles themselves.
Christian writers came to give her a title for it: apostle to the apostles. Apostle means one who is sent.
In 2016 Pope Francis raised her day, July 22, from a memorial to a feast, the same rank as the feasts of the apostles, and the decree used that old title.

how: Catholics celebrate the Feast of Saint Mary Magdalene on July 22, with the Gloria at Mass and her encounter with the risen Jesus read as the Gospel.

o: a follower who studies at a teacher's feet
one who is sent, as Mary was sent to tell
one of the twelve men, and only them

games.q: the garden tomb — tap the pairs.
p: see the cloths and go home

s: Mary recognizes Jesus as soon as she sees him
she thinks he's the gardener until he says her name.
noli me tangere may mean don't cling to me
the Greek suggests not holding on; she's sent to tell the others.
Mary Magdalene's day became a feast in 2016
Pope Francis raised July 22 from a memorial to a feast.

games.q: you're Mary Magdalene. the man you took for the gardener has just said your name, and it's Jesus. what does he tell you to do?
o: stay with him in the garden.
games.why: he sends her: go to my brethren. she comes and tells the disciples, I have seen the Lord.

practice: Think back over the last week or so for something genuinely good: a recovery, a kindness you saw, a small win, a reconciliation, a baby, a sunrise, and let it fill your chest for a moment.
Then think of who would be glad to hear it, and picture their face. If you pray, hold Mary's words, I have seen the Lord, and give thanks; if you don't, just enjoy the good news.

wordCard.voice: Apostle. One who is sent: the title given to Mary Magdalene after Jesus sent her to tell the disciples he was risen. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: apostle, one who is sent, from apostellō, to send.

carryVoice: Your line: I have seen the lord. The first one sent was the one who stayed. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Jesus saith to her: Mary. She turning, saith to him: Rabboni (which is to say, Master).

sources.ref: Decree on the celebration of St. Mary Magdalene (2016)
